claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm hoping to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, their eligibility depends on their current situation. Could you please tell me whether Alex is currently in any of the following:

- Approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)
- Approved training (such as an unpaid government-approved training course)
- Neither of the above

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Just a couple more questions about Alex's situation:

Is Alex studying his A-levels on a full-time basis (i.e., more than 12 hours per week of supervised study or course-related work)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's doing full-time A-levels - it's definitely more than 12 hours a week with all his classes and coursework.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

One more question about Alex: Is he registered with his education provider or a careers service? In England, this would typically mean being enrolled with his school or college. This is a requirement for young people aged 16-19 in approved education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, of course - he's enrolled at his sixth form college where he's doing the A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Are you responsible for Alex, meaning he lives with you and you're responsible for his day-to-day care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**Alex (age 18):** ✅ Eligible
- Although Alex is over 16, Child Benefit can continue until a young person turns 20 if they remain in approved full-time education
- A-levels are an approved qualification
- Alex is studying full-time (more than 12 hours per week)
- He is properly enrolled at his sixth form college
- He lives with you and you are responsible for him
- You are a UK resident

You can continue to claim Child Benefit for Alex until he finishes his A-levels, or until he turns 20 (whichever comes first). If his education or training status changes, you would need to inform the Child Benefit Office.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

Additionally, the claimant is responsible for Alex as he lives at home with them, and the claimant resides in the UK. All eligibility criteria are therefore met.
